title: Playing with Al Hirt at Dan's International on Bourbon Street
summary: Netto describes the Bourbon Street club job with Jumbo, Bob Havens' long choruses, and Hirt's fast tempos.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well you played with these bands when they came through. Did you travel with any of them? No, no, no.

So you stayed in town. In fact, I think I fell out with Al Hurt on the same deal when I played with Jumbo. Where did you play with Jumbo? Huh? Where did you play with him? I played with him when they opened up with Dan Levy's down there in that, what they called it, place on Bourbon Street there, that was one of my few stints on Bourbon Street. Toulouse and Bourbon? Yeah, he called it, not his club, the one before. Next door was a Chinese restaurant. Dan's International.
Dan's International, right. It was a Chinese restaurant, but I don't remember the name of the club.

The club was a ... I can find it, huh? They had nets on the bandstand and everything else and we had a black jacket. It wasn't something like Bayou. No, but it had something to that ... It was that kind of thing.
I know the Bayou Ball was in the wall of the Montietran or something.

I can't think of a ton of them. And whatchacar was playing for a bone in there and damn he was fine. And that guy would, well ... Oh, Bob Haven? Bob Haven, yeah. He played down there with him. Jumbo would take 30 choruses and Bob would take 40.
And the bass player would work in, work in, work in.

And then when he'd get finished, he'd say, take a cup. And he says, four beats, four beats, Frank, four beats. I said, for Christ's sake you're playing so fast I can't even play two. I said, whatchacar am I going to be playing? One.
